title: Check: Reactions of Acids with Metals (2)

questions.stem: What is the test for hydrogen gas?

options.text: Bubble it through limewater and it turns milky
Hold a glowing splint and it relights
Hold a burning splint and hear a squeaky pop
Add universal indicator and it turns green

questions.explanation: The test for hydrogen gas is to hold a burning splint near the gas. If hydrogen is present, it burns with a characteristic 'squeaky pop' sound. This small explosion occurs because hydrogen reacts with oxygen in the air: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.

questions.stem: Which of these metals reacts most vigorously with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is the most reactive of these metals and reacts vigorously with dilute HCl, producing rapid bubbling and the metal disappearing quickly. Zinc reacts moderately, iron reacts slowly, and copper does not react at all as it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.
